output.brief:
I can't yet tell you whether the rota caused the rise in falls, so I wouldn't reverse it now. The rise has at least two plausible explanations, and the evidence doesn't separate them.

First, recording changed on 1 July. The two homes moved to the app, and the other seven homes still use paper. Staff say unharmed "found on floor" cases were under-written before. A check of Q2 handover notes found three clear unreported falls and three ambiguous ones. The increase is mostly no-harm and unwitnessed falls. Harm falls rose only from 6 to 9.

Second, the rota may be a real factor. Night falls rose, and Ashby Fold's median night call answer time is 3 min 40 s. There is no pre-June baseline, so I can't say calls are slower. Penmor Lodge has no answer-time data at all.

Falls per 1,000 bed days are inside the control limits. Other homes have had similar one-quarter jumps that reversed. But a real 40% increase would take two to three quarters to show.

Medication changes and frailer admissions are untested.

Next steps: keep the pilot running under its existing pause criteria. Show falls as rates, with the recording change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell answer times. Review in late January with Q4 data. Don't discipline night staff, and don't withdraw the app.
